note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII Physics board exam 2026, Q.P. code 55/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Q25 and the network-diagram alternative of Q22, which depend on circuit figures, are left out; other figures are described in words. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a region, the electric potential varies as V = 10 − 50x, where V is in volts and x in metres. The electric field in the region is :
questions.solution: E = −dV/dx = +50 V/m, i.e. 50 N/C along +x.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A conducting wire connects two charged metallic spheres A and B of radii r₁ and r₂ respectively. The distance between the spheres is very large compared to their radii. The ratio of electric fields (E_A/E_B) at the surfaces of spheres A and B will be
questions.solution: Connected spheres are at the same potential V = kq/r, and the surface field is E = kq/r² = V/r. So E_A/E_B = r₂/r₁.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A long straight wire of circular cross-section (radius a) carries a steady current I. The current is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The magnitude of the magnetic field produced at a point at a distance a/2 from the axis of the wire will be
questions.solution: Inside the wire B = μ₀Ir/(2πa²). At r = a/2: B = μ₀I/(4πa).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The shape of the interference fringes in Young's double-slit experiment, when the distance between the slits and the screen is very large compared to the slit separation, is nearly
questions.solution: The fringes are strictly hyperbolic, but for D ≫ d they are nearly straight lines.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An electromagnetic wave passes from vacuum into a dielectric medium with relative electrical permittivity 3/2 and relative magnetic permeability 8/3. Then its
options: wavelength is doubled and frequency remains unchanged.
wavelength is doubled and frequency is halved.
wavelength is halved and frequency remains unchanged.
wavelength and frequency both will remain unchanged.
questions.solution: n = √(εᵣμᵣ) = √4 = 2. Frequency does not change; speed and wavelength are halved.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a series LCR circuit, the voltage across the resistor, capacitor and inductor is 10 V each. If the capacitor is short circuited, the voltage across the inductor will be
questions.solution: Equal voltages mean R = X_L = X_C, and the supply voltage is 10 V. Without the capacitor Z = √2 R, so I = 10/(√2R) and V_L = I X_L = 10/√2 = 5√2 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Electromagnetic waves used in a diagnostic tool in medicine have a wavelength range
questions.solution: X-rays, used in medical diagnosis, have wavelengths of about 1 nm to 10⁻³ nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The 'distance of closest approach' of an alpha particle is d when it moves with a velocity v head-on towards the target nucleus. If the velocity of the alpha particle is halved, the new distance of closest approach will be
questions.solution: d = 2kZe²/(½mv²) ∝ 1/v², so halving v makes it 4d.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A concave lens of focal length 10 cm is cut into two identical plano-concave lenses. The focal length of each lens will be
questions.solution: Each half has only one curved surface, so its power is halved and its focal length doubles to 20 cm (a diverging lens).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Four independent waves are expressed as (i) y₁ = A₁ sin ωt (ii) y₂ = A₂ sin 2ωt (iii) y₃ = A₃ cos ωt (iv) y₄ = A₄ sin(ωt + π/3). Interference between two of these waves is possible in
questions.solution: Sustained interference needs the same frequency and a constant phase difference; (i), (iii) and (iv) all have frequency ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two heaters rated (P₁, V) and (P₂, V) are connected in series across a dc source of V/2 volt. The power consumed by the combination will be
questions.solution: R₁ = V²/P₁, R₂ = V²/P₂. P = (V/2)²/(R₁ + R₂) = (V²/4)/(V²(1/P₁ + 1/P₂)) = P₁P₂/(4(P₁ + P₂)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In an unbiased p-n junction, at equilibrium, which of the following statements is true?
options: Diffusion current is zero but drift current exists.
Diffusion current exists but drift current is zero.
Diffusion and drift currents are equal and opposite.
Both the diffusion and drift currents exist but are unequal.
questions.solution: At equilibrium the diffusion current is balanced by an equal and opposite drift current, so the net current is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): All atoms have a net magnetic moment.
Reason (R): A current loop does not always behave as a magnetic dipole.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.solution: Atoms of diamagnetic substances have zero net magnetic moment, so A is false. A current loop always behaves as a magnetic dipole, so R is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If accelerated electrons are passed through a narrow slit, a diffraction pattern is observed.
Reason (R): Electrons behave as both particles and waves.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.solution: Electrons have a de Broglie wavelength, so they diffract; R explains A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The mass of a nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of the constituent nucleons.
Reason (R): Energy is absorbed when the nucleons are bound together to form a nucleus.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.solution: A is true (mass defect). R is false: energy (the binding energy) is released when the nucleus forms.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, the energy levels are discrete and quantised.
Reason (R): In a hydrogen atom, the electrostatic force on the electron provides the necessary centripetal force for it to revolve around the nucleus.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.solution: Both are true, but quantisation comes from the angular momentum condition mvr = nh/2π, not from the electrostatic force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text: In a photoelectric experiment, the emitter plate is irradiated with radiation of 200 nm. The photocurrent becomes zero when the collector plate potential is −0.80 V. Calculate the work function (in eV) of the emitter.
questions.solution: Photon energy = 1240/200 eV = 6.2 eV. Kmax = eV₀ = 0.80 eV. Work function = 6.2 − 0.8 = 5.4 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A beam of light consisting of two wavelengths 400 nm and 600 nm is used to illuminate a single slit of width 1 mm. Find the least distance from the central maximum where the dark fringes due to both wavelengths coincide on a screen placed 1.5 m from the slit.
questions.solution: Minima are at y = nλD/a. They coincide when n₁(400) = n₂(600), first at n₁ = 3, n₂ = 2 (path 1200 nm). y = 1200 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.5/10⁻³ = 1.8 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a Young's double-slit set-up with slit separation 0.6 mm, a beam of light consisting of two wavelengths 440 nm and 660 nm is used to obtain an interference pattern on a screen kept 1.5 m in front of the slits. Find the least distance from the central maximum where the bright fringes due to both wavelengths coincide.
questions.solution: Bright fringes at y = nλD/d coincide when n₁(440) = n₂(660), first at n₁ = 3, n₂ = 2 (1320 nm). y = 1320 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.5/(0.6 × 10⁻³) = 3.3 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire of length L is bent into (i) a square coil having N turns and (ii) a circular coil having N turns. The coil in both cases is free to turn about a vertical axis in the plane of the coil, in a uniform horizontal magnetic field, and carries the same current. Find the ratio of the maximum torque acting on the square coil to that on the circular coil.
questions.solution: τ_max = NIAB, so the ratio is the ratio of areas. Square: side L/(4N), area L²/(16N²). Circle: radius L/(2πN), area L²/(4πN²). Ratio = (1/16)/(1/(4π)) = π/4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: What is the order of magnitude of the drift velocity of electrons in a conductor? Deduce the relation between the current flowing through a conductor and the drift velocity of electrons in it.
questions.solution: About 10⁻⁴ m/s (a fraction of a mm per second). In a conductor of cross-section A with n free electrons per unit volume, the charge crossing a section in time t is (nAv_d t)e. So I = q/t = neAv_d.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Draw the plot of the potential energy of a pair of nucleons as a function of their separation. Write two important conclusions that can be drawn from this plot.
questions.solution: The curve is steeply positive (repulsive) for separations below about 0.8 fm, has a minimum (most negative) near 0.8 fm, and rises towards zero by a few fm. Conclusions: the nuclear force is attractive and strong for separations of about 0.8 to a few fm; it becomes strongly repulsive below about 0.8 fm; it is short ranged and negligible beyond a few fm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Using Gauss's law, deduce an expression for the electric field at a point due to a uniformly charged infinite plane thin sheet.
(b) Two large thin plane sheets, each having surface charge density σ, are held close and parallel to each other in air. What is the net electric field at a point (i) inside and (ii) outside the sheets?
questions.solution: (a) Take a cylindrical Gaussian surface of cross-section A through the sheet. Flux passes only through the two flat ends: 2EA = σA/ε₀, so E = σ/(2ε₀), perpendicular to the sheet. (b) Each sheet gives σ/(2ε₀) pointing away from it. (i) Between the sheets the fields cancel: E = 0. (ii) Outside they add: E = σ/ε₀.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C has a dielectric slab between its plates. It is charged to a potential difference V by connecting it across a battery. The battery is then disconnected. If the dielectric slab is now withdrawn from the capacitor, how will the following be affected? (a) Capacitance of the capacitor (b) Energy stored in the capacitor (c) The potential difference between the plates. Justify your answer in each case.
questions.solution: With the battery disconnected, the charge Q stays constant. (a) C decreases K times (C′ = C/K) because the dielectric is removed. (b) U = Q²/(2C) increases K times; the extra energy comes from the work done in pulling out the slab. (c) V = Q/C increases K times.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A narrow beam of electrons enters with a velocity of 3 × 10⁷ m/s symmetrically through the space between two parallel horizontal plates kept 2 cm apart. If each plate is 3 cm long, calculate the potential difference V applied between the plates so that the beam just strikes the end of the lower plate.
questions.solution: The beam must be deflected y = 1 cm while crossing L = 3 cm. Time t = L/v = 0.03/(3 × 10⁷) = 10⁻⁹ s. y = ½at² gives a = 2 × 0.01/10⁻¹⁸ = 2 × 10¹⁶ m/s². E = ma/e = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ × 2 × 10¹⁶/1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 1.14 × 10⁵ V/m. V = Ed = 1.14 × 10⁵ × 0.02 ≈ 2.3 × 10³ V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Briefly explain the two important processes that occur during the formation of a p-n junction.
questions.solution: Diffusion: holes diffuse from the p-side to the n-side and electrons from n to p because of the concentration difference, leaving behind immobile ions and forming the depletion layer. Drift: the electric field of these ions (barrier potential) drives minority carriers across the junction in the opposite direction. At equilibrium the diffusion current equals the drift current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Draw the ray diagram to show image formation by a refracting telescope and write the expression for angular magnification for the telescope in normal adjustment.
(b) Give two reasons to explain why a reflecting telescope is preferred over a refracting telescope.
questions.solution: (a) Parallel rays from a distant object pass through the objective (long focal length f₀) and form a real, inverted image at its focus, which is also the focus of the eyepiece (f_e); the final image is at infinity. Magnification m = f₀/f_e. (b) A mirror has no chromatic aberration; a parabolic mirror removes spherical aberration; a large mirror is lighter, cheaper and can be supported from behind, giving more light-gathering power and resolution.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) State the two conditions under which total internal reflection occurs.
(b) A transparent container holds layers of three immiscible transparent liquids, A at the bottom, B above it and C at the top, with refractive indices n, (3/4)n and (2/3)n respectively. A laser beam in A is incident at the interface between A and B at an angle θ. Prove that the beam does not enter region C at all for sin θ ≥ 2/3.
questions.solution: (a) Light must travel from a denser to a rarer medium, and the angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle. (b) The interfaces are parallel, so by Snell's law n sin θ = (3/4)n sin r₁ = (2/3)n sin r₂. Hence sin r₂ = (3/2) sin θ. If sin θ ≥ 2/3, sin r₂ ≥ 1: no refraction is possible at the B-C interface, the beam is totally reflected and never enters C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
A galvanometer is used to detect or measure small currents in an electrical circuit. It works on the fact that a current-carrying coil experiences a deflecting torque when placed in a magnetic field. The deflection is related to the current in the coil, the number of turns, the area of the coil and the magnetic field. A hair spring attached to the coil provides a counter torque and helps in measuring the deflection. A galvanometer can be converted to an ammeter or a voltmeter of desired range by using suitable resistances.

The torque on the coil remains constant irrespective of the coil's orientation during rotation due to
options: use of soft iron core which increases the magnetic field
hair spring which provides the counter torque
eddy current in the iron core which causes damping
questions.solution: In a radial field the plane of the coil is always parallel to B, so τ = NIAB at every orientation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
A galvanometer is used to detect or measure small currents in an electrical circuit. It works on the fact that a current-carrying coil experiences a deflecting torque when placed in a magnetic field. The deflection is related to the current in the coil, the number of turns, the area of the coil and the magnetic field. A hair spring attached to the coil provides a counter torque and helps in measuring the deflection. A galvanometer can be converted to an ammeter or a voltmeter of desired range by using suitable resistances.

The best way to increase the current sensitivity of a galvanometer is by
options: increasing number of turns of the coil
increasing area of coil and magnetic field strength
decreasing area of coil and magnetic field strength
increasing torsional constant of the hair spring
questions.solution: Current sensitivity θ/I = NAB/k. Increasing A and B raises it without increasing the coil's resistance, as adding turns would (portal's answer).

A galvanometer is used to detect or measure small currents in an electrical circuit. It works on the fact that a current-carrying coil experiences a deflecting torque when placed in a magnetic field. The deflection is related to the current in the coil, the number of turns, the area of the coil and the magnetic field. A hair spring attached to the coil provides a counter torque and helps in measuring the deflection. A galvanometer can be converted to an ammeter or a voltmeter of desired range by using suitable resistances.

A galvanometer with coil resistance 20 Ω shows full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA. To convert it into an ammeter of range (0 − 10 A), a resistance of
options: 0.05 Ω should be connected in series with it.
0.05 Ω should be connected in parallel with it.
0.01 Ω should be connected in parallel with it.
0.01 Ω should be connected in series with it.
questions.solution: Shunt S = I_gG/(I − I_g) = 0.005 × 20/9.995 ≈ 0.01 Ω, in parallel.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
A researcher performs an experiment on the photoelectric effect using two metals A and B with unknown work functions. She illuminates A and B with monochromatic radiation of various frequencies and records the corresponding stopping potentials Vₛ. The graph of Vₛ against frequency ν gives two parallel straight lines: line A cuts the frequency axis at ν₁ and line B at ν₂ (ν₂ > ν₁); extended backwards, they cut the Vₛ axis at −V₁ and −V₂ respectively.

From the graph, the work functions of A and B are (h is Planck's constant and e the charge on an electron)
questions.solution: Work function φ₀ = hν₀, where ν₀ is the threshold frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
A researcher performs an experiment on the photoelectric effect using two metals A and B with unknown work functions. She illuminates A and B with monochromatic radiation of various frequencies and records the corresponding stopping potentials Vₛ. The graph of Vₛ against frequency ν gives two parallel straight lines: line A cuts the frequency axis at ν₁ and line B at ν₂ (ν₂ > ν₁); extended backwards, they cut the Vₛ axis at −V₁ and −V₂ respectively.

For radiation of frequency ν > ν₂ incident on the surfaces of A and B, the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected electrons is
options: greater for metal A because it has a smaller work function.
greater for metal B because it has a larger work function.
greater for metal B because it has higher threshold frequency.
the same for both metals because it is independent of work functions.
questions.solution: Kmax = hν − φ₀ is larger for the metal with the smaller work function, A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
A researcher performs an experiment on the photoelectric effect using two metals A and B with unknown work functions. She illuminates A and B with monochromatic radiation of various frequencies and records the corresponding stopping potentials Vₛ. The graph of Vₛ against frequency ν gives two parallel straight lines: line A cuts the frequency axis at ν₁ and line B at ν₂ (ν₂ > ν₁); extended backwards, they cut the Vₛ axis at −V₁ and −V₂ respectively.

If the intensity of the incident radiation for both metals A and B is doubled keeping its frequency constant, then
options: the slope of the parallel lines will increase.
the slope of the parallel lines will decrease.
the threshold frequencies for both A and B will decrease.
the slope of the parallel lines will not change but more electrons will be emitted per second.
questions.solution: The slope h/e and the thresholds do not depend on intensity; only the number of photoelectrons increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
A researcher performs an experiment on the photoelectric effect using two metals A and B with unknown work functions. She illuminates A and B with monochromatic radiation of various frequencies and records the corresponding stopping potentials Vₛ. The graph of Vₛ against frequency ν gives two parallel straight lines: line A cuts the frequency axis at ν₁ and line B at ν₂ (ν₂ > ν₁); extended backwards, they cut the Vₛ axis at −V₁ and −V₂ respectively.

The threshold frequency for a metal surface is ν₀. If radiation of frequency 3ν₀ illuminates the surface, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is E₁. If the frequency is increased to 6ν₀, it becomes E₂. Then E₁/E₂ equals
questions.solution: E₁ = h(3ν₀ − ν₀) = 2hν₀ and E₂ = 5hν₀, so E₁/E₂ = 2/5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
A researcher performs an experiment on the photoelectric effect using two metals A and B with unknown work functions. She illuminates A and B with monochromatic radiation of various frequencies and records the corresponding stopping potentials Vₛ. The graph of Vₛ against frequency ν gives two parallel straight lines: line A cuts the frequency axis at ν₁ and line B at ν₂ (ν₂ > ν₁); extended backwards, they cut the Vₛ axis at −V₁ and −V₂ respectively.

Let m be the slope of the graph line for metal B. If e is the electron charge, then Planck's constant h is given by
questions.solution: The slope is h/e, so h = me.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) An electric dipole consists of two point charges q and −q separated by a distance 2a. Derive an expression for the electric field E due to this dipole at a point distant r from the centre of the dipole on the equatorial plane. Write the expression for the electric field at a far off point, i.e. r ≫ a.
(b) A dipole is placed in the x-y plane such that charges q and −q are located at x = a and x = b respectively. There exists an electric field E = 2î N/C in the region. Calculate the force F and torque τ experienced by the dipole.
questions.solution: (a) Each charge is at distance √(r² + a²) and gives a field of magnitude kq/(r² + a²). The components along the perpendicular bisector cancel; the components parallel to the dipole axis add: E = 2kq a/(r² + a²)^(3/2) = kp/(r² + a²)^(3/2), directed opposite to p (p = 2aq). For r ≫ a: E = kp/r³ = p/(4πε₀r³), opposite to p. (b) In a uniform field the forces qE and −qE cancel: F = 0. The dipole moment p = q(a − b)î is along the field, so τ = p × E = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Two cells of emf E₁ and E₂ with internal resistances r₁ and r₂ respectively are connected in parallel (positive terminals together and negative terminals together). Deduce expressions for the equivalent emf and equivalent internal resistance of the combination.
(b) A parallel combination, as in (a), of two cells of emfs E and 3E and internal resistances R each is connected across a resistance 2R. Find the current that flows through resistance 2R.
questions.solution: (a) With common terminal voltage V: I₁ = (E₁ − V)/r₁, I₂ = (E₂ − V)/r₂ and I = I₁ + I₂. Solving, V = (E₁r₂ + E₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂) − I r₁r₂/(r₁ + r₂). So E_eq = (E₁r₂ + E₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂) and r_eq = r₁r₂/(r₁ + r₂). (b) E_eq = (ER + 3ER)/(2R) = 2E, r_eq = R/2. I = 2E/(2R + R/2) = 4E/(5R).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Using the relation for refraction at a curved spherical surface, derive the expression for the lens maker's formula.
(b) Three lenses L₁, L₂ and L₃, each of focal length 40 cm, are placed coaxially. The distance between L₁ and L₂ is 120 cm and between L₂ and L₃ is 20 cm. An object is kept 80 cm to the left of L₁. Find the distance of the final image formed from the object.
questions.solution: (a) Refraction at the first surface (radius R₁): n₂/v₁ − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R₁. The image acts as the object for the second surface (R₂): n₁/v − n₂/v₁ = (n₁ − n₂)/R₂. Adding, n₁(1/v − 1/u) = (n₂ − n₁)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). For an object at infinity v = f: 1/f = (n₂₁ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). (b) Taking the lenses as convex: L₁: u = −80, 1/v = 1/40 − 1/80, v = 80 cm. This image is 40 cm before L₂, at its focus, so L₂ sends out parallel rays. L₃ focuses them 40 cm beyond it. Distance from the object = 80 + 120 + 20 + 40 = 260 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation by a concave mirror when the object is kept between its focus and the centre of curvature. Using this diagram, derive the mirror formula.
(b) A concave mirror produces a two times magnified virtual image of an object kept 10 cm in front of it. Calculate the focal length of the mirror.
questions.solution: (a) The image is real, inverted, magnified and beyond C. From similar triangles A′B′F ~ MPF and A′B′P ~ ABP: B′A′/BA = B′F/FP = B′P/BP. With sign convention (v − f)/f = v/u, which rearranges to 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. (b) Virtual image, m = +2 = −v/u with u = −10 cm, so v = +20 cm. 1/f = 1/20 − 1/10 = −1/20, f = −20 cm (focal length 20 cm).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
(b) Derive an expression for the self-inductance of an air-filled long solenoid of length l and cross-sectional area A having N turns.
(c) A conducting rod of length 50 cm, with one end pivoted, is rotated with an angular speed of 60 rpm in a uniform magnetic field of 4.0 mT directed perpendicular to the plane of rotation of the rod. Find the emf induced in the rod.
questions.solution: (a) The induced emf in a circuit equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through it: ε = −dΦ/dt (the sign is Lenz's law). (b) B = μ₀(N/l)I inside, so total flux linkage NΦ = N(μ₀NI/l)A. L = NΦ/I = μ₀N²A/l. (c) ω = 2π rad/s. ε = ½Bωl² = ½ × 4 × 10⁻³ × 2π × 0.25 ≈ 3.14 × 10⁻³ V = 3.14 mV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer. State the principle on which it works and obtain the ratio of secondary voltage to primary voltage in terms of the number of turns and the currents in the two coils.
(b) The ratio of the number of turns in the primary to the secondary of an ideal transformer is 1 : 5. If 5 kW power at 200 V is supplied to the primary, find (i) the current in the primary and (ii) the output voltage.
questions.solution: (a) Two coils on a laminated soft iron core, the secondary with more turns. Principle: mutual induction; the alternating flux of the primary links the secondary. The same flux change per turn gives Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ, and for an ideal transformer VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ, so Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ = Iₚ/Iₛ. (b) (i) Iₚ = 5000/200 = 25 A. (ii) Vₛ = 5 × 200 = 1000 V.
